title: Daemon distributable — tarball with bundled ws + node-pty, assume Node 20 on target
decision: The remote-installable daemon ships as a gzipped tar file (`switchboard-daemon-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz`, ~176 KB) built by `scripts/build-daemon-tarball.sh` and produced by the `dist:daemon-tarball` npm script. Contents: `dist/daemon/` (compiled TS), `node_modules/ws/` (pure JS), and `node_modules/node-pty/` including the linux-x64 native prebuild (`build/Release/pty.node`) that our AppImage build already produces via `@electron/rebuild`. Target hosts must have `node` version 20.x on `$PATH` — v1 does not bundle Node, and the ABI-locked prebuild is not compatible with Node 22+ without a rebuild.

context.task_description: Sprint 21 needs to install a runnable daemon on a fresh Linux host over SSH.
assumptions: Target hosts in v1 are Linux x86_64 with systemd --user available
Node 20 is broadly available on target hosts (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 12+, RHEL 9, Fedora 38+ ship or have easy access to it)
Ballooning the AppImage with a bundled 60-80 MB Node runtime for a feature only some users will invoke is not worth it in v1
electron-builder's @electron/rebuild step gives us a Node-20-ABI-compatible pty.node for free during our normal AppImage build

options.label: Tarball with bundled deps, assume system Node 20 (chosen)
options.description: Smallest artifact (~176 KB). Reuses build artifacts we already produce. Zero new build-time tooling. Constraint: exact Node ABI match required — Node 22 needs a separate prebuild variant.

options.label: Standalone daemon binary via pkg / nexe / bun compile
options.description: Single-file drop-in, no Node dependency on target. Rejected for v1: adds ~60 MB per binary, introduces a new build-chain dependency (pkg is unmaintained; nexe and bun-compile have their own gotchas), and native modules like node-pty need per-target-arch rebuilds either way.

options.label: Pure scp of source, `npm install` on the target
options.description: Simplest client-side. Rejected: requires build tools (make, g++, python) on the target for node-pty compilation, which many minimal server images lack. Also multiplies install time from ~5s to ~60s.

options.label: Bundled Node in the tarball
options.description: Removes the Node-20 requirement. Rejected for v1: quadruples the tarball size (~60 MB vs. 176 KB) and adds a second binary we would need to keep current on security patches. Reconsider if the Node-20 constraint bites real users.

rationale: The narrowest artifact that ships the daemon in a runnable state is the winner for a first cut — we can broaden compatibility later without changing the on-target file layout. Node 20 is the current LTS through April 2026 (matches Electron 33's ABI, matches Ubuntu 24.04's default) and can be installed on any target with nodesource or a package manager. When we hit a real user on Node 22, we build a second prebuild variant and pick the right one at install time; when we hit a target without any Node, we ship a bundled-Node variant. Both are incremental changes to this same tarball-based flow.

risk.rollback: Delete scripts/build-daemon-tarball.sh and the dist:daemon-tarball script; regenerate as a standalone binary or a source-only tarball as needed. The remote-provisioner treats the artifact as an opaque bundle.

outcome.notes: Verification: tarball extracts and daemon starts without ABI errors under Node 20 on target Ubuntu VM. Live provisioning completes step 7 (daemon becomes ready).
